title: Retrieval and Ranking
description: Improve retrieval quality with filtering, hybrid search, reranking, and metadata-aware queries in C#.

blocks.text: Retrieval quality often matters more than model choice. A strong retriever with a small model can outperform a giant model with weak retrieval. In C# backends, retrieval logic is the highest-leverage place to improve answers.

blocks.title: Techniques for stronger retrieval
items: **Top-k filtering** — return the k most similar chunks.
**Metadata filtering** — restrict by tenant, category, date, or authorization rules before ranking.
**Hybrid search** — combine vector similarity with keyword or BM25 search.
**Reranking** — send top candidates to a cross-encoder or reranker and sort again.
**Parent-child retrieval** — retrieve a small chunk but return a larger surrounding passage for context.

blocks.title: Hybrid retrieval with Azure AI Search
blocks.content: Full async method with filters, cancellation token, and sample usage.

blocks.title: Security and retrieval
blocks.text: Always apply authorization filters before semantic ranking. A user should never see another tenant's chunks, even if they are semantically close.

items.text: I can describe the difference between retrieval and ranking
items.hint: Retrieval fetches candidates; ranking reorders them for relevance

items.text: I know why metadata filtering is a security control
items.hint: It enforces tenant or role boundaries before retrieval results are returned

items.text: I can explain hybrid search in one sentence
items.hint: It combines semantic search with keyword or BM25 search to improve recall

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Retrieval quality usually matters more than model choice.
Hybrid search, filtering, and reranking each improve different failure modes.
Security filters must run before semantic ranking.
blocks.takeaway: Treat retrieval as a first-class feature. Measure precision and recall with real user queries, not synthetic benchmarks.
